readme: # LogicDiff: LLM-Guided Compress–Generate–Restore for Trustworthy Tabular Synthesis LogicDiff builds on the official TabDDPM implementation (“TabDDPM: Modelling Tabular Data with Diffusion Models” [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.15421)). ## $${\color[RGB]{18, 119, 211}\Huge\text{Fantastic Four}}$$ Mohamed Khalil - khali178@umn.edu Nitish Poojari - pooja011@umn.edu Tyler Chan - chen7751@umn.edu Weifu Li - li003454@umn.edu ## Setup the environment 1. Install [conda](https://docs.conda.io/en/latest/miniconda.html) (just to manage the env). 2. Run the following commands ```bash export REPO_DIR=/path/to/the/code cd $REPO_DIR conda create -n tabmdm python=3.9.7 conda activate tabmdm pip install torch==1.10.1+cu111 -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html pip install -r requirements.txt # if the following commands do not succeed, update conda conda env config vars set PYTHONPATH=${PYTHONPATH}:${REPO_DIR} conda env config vars set PROJECT_DIR=${REPO_DIR} conda deactivate conda activate tabmdm ``` ### Datasets To download the datasets, run: ``` bash conda activate tddpm cd $PROJECT_DIR wget "https://www.dropbox.com/s/rpckvcs3vx7j605/data.tar?dl=0" -O data.tar tar -xvf data.tar ``` ### File structure `tab-ddpm/` -- implementation of the proposed method `tuned_models/` -- tuned hyperparameters of evaluation model (CatBoost or MLP) LLM compression folder (`llm/`): - Utilities to compress a raw CSV/Parquet into a core dataset and metadata. - `make_dataset_compressed.py` runs the full pipeline and generates schema. json, relations.json,compression_meta.json, and X_c.npy. - `llm_to_relations.py` extracts RH (hierarchy), RM (math), and RT (temporal) rules into relations.json. - If `config.toml` is produced, it is an auto-generated training config template; see CONFIG_DESCRIPTION.md. All main scripts are in `scripts/` folder: - `scripts/pipeline.py` are used to train, sample and eval TabDDPM using a given config - `scripts/tune_ddpm.py` -- tune hyperparameters of TabDDPM - `scripts/eval_[catboost|mlp|simple].py` -- evaluate synthetic data using a tuned evaluation model or simple models - `scripts/eval_seeds.py` -- eval using multiple sampling and multuple eval seeds - `scripts/eval_seeds_simple.py` -- eval using multiple sampling and multuple eval seeds (for simple models) - `scripts/tune_evaluation_model.py` -- tune hyperparameters of eval model (CatBoost or MLP) - `scripts/resample_privacy.py` -- privacy calculation - `scripts/restore_table.py` -- restore a compressed dataset back to the original column space using compression_meta.json - `scripts/validate_restorer.py` -- round-trip check: compressed arrays → restored CSV → re-encoded arrays - `scripts/compute_dcr.py` -- compute DCR-style privacy metric between real and synthetic datasets Comprehensive analysis (`comprehensive_analysis.py`): - `comprehensive_analysis.py` -- end-to-end evaluation script that generates summary plots and metrics (WD/JS/correlation L2, plus optional TSTR utility via CatBoost) for a given --dataset and --exp directory Experiments folder (`exp/`): - All results and synthetic data are stored in `exp/[ds_name]/[exp_name]/` folder - `exp/[ds_name]/config.toml` is a base config for tuning TabDDPM - `exp/[ds_name]/eval_[catboost|mlp].json` stores results of evaluation (`scripts/eval_seeds.py`) To understand the structure of `config.toml` file, read `CONFIG_DESCRIPTION.md`. Baselines: - `CTAB-GAN/` -- [official repo](https://github.com/Team-TUD/CTAB-GAN) - `CTAB-GAN-Plus/` -- [official repo](https://github.com/Team-TUD/CTAB-GAN-Plus) ### Examples Run LLM Compression Example: ```bash python make_dataset_compressed.py --data insurance.csv --schema schema.json --model "models/gemini-2.5-flash" --do-split ``` Need to pass Google Gemini API key as well otherwise it should be in the ```os.getenv```, if not the program will fail. Example with API key: ``` bash python make_dataset_compressed.py --data insurance.csv --schema schema.json --model "models/gemini-2.5-flash" --api-key "API_KEY_HERE" --do-split ``` Schema.json should be created by user with descriptions of the columns along with the target column. The format should be as such: ```json { "columns": [ {"name": "age", "dtype": "float", "desc": "age is a numeric quantity. min=18, max=64"}, {"name": "sex", "dtype": "categorical", "desc": "sex is a categorical/text field. examples=['male','female']"}, {"name": "bmi", "dtype": "float", "desc": "bmi is a numeric quantity. min=15.96, max=53.13"}, {"name": "children", "dtype": "float", "desc": "children is a numeric quantity. min=0, max=5"}, {"name": "smoker", "dtype": "categorical", "desc": "smoker is a categorical/text field. examples=['no','yes']"}, {"name": "region", "dtype": "categorical", "desc": "region is a categorical/text field. examples=['southeast','southwest','northwest']"}, {"name": "charges", "dtype": "float", "desc": "charges is a numeric quantity. min=1121.87, max=63770.42"} ], "target": "charges" } ``` If no schema.json file is provided, then calling the program requires target to be specified as such: ```bash python make_dataset_compressed.py --data insurance.csv --target "charges" --model "models/gemini-2.5-flash" --do-split ``` Run TabDDPM tuning. Template and example (`--eval_seeds` is optional): ```bash python scripts/tune_ddpm.py [ds_name] [train_size] synthetic [catboost|mlp] [exp_name] --eval_seeds python scripts/tune_ddpm.py churn2 6500 synthetic catboost ddpm_tune --eval_seeds ``` Run TabDDPM pipeline. Template and example (`--train`, `--sample`, `--eval` are optional): ```bash python scripts/pipeline.py --config [path_to_your_config] --train --sample --eval python scripts/pipeline.py --config exp/churn2/ddpm_md4_smart_norm/config.toml --train --sample ``` It takes approximately 7min to run the script above (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti). Run evaluation over seeds Before running evaluation, you have to train the model with the given hyperparameters (the example above). Template and example: ```bash python scripts/eval_seeds.py --config [path_to_your_config] [n_eval_seeds] [ddpm|smote|ctabgan|ctabgan-plus|tvae] synthetic [catboost|mlp] [n_sample_seeds] python scripts/eval_seeds.py --config exp/churn2/ddpm_md4_smart_norm/config.toml 10 ddpm synthetic catboost 5 ``` Run some analysis Runs the comprehensive evaluation on an experiment folder, including distribution plots and summary metrics. You can optionally run downstream utility (TSTR) using CatBoost/MLP. example: ```bash python comprehensive_analysis.py --dataset adult --exp ddpm_md4_smart_norm --use-catboost --use-mlp --catboost-task-type CPU --torch-device cuda:0 ``` Outputs (written under `exp/[dataset]/[exp]/`): - `numeric_distributions.png` — real vs synthetic numeric feature distributions - `categorical_distributions.png` — real vs synthetic categorical feature distributions - `summary_metrics.csv` — aggregated metrics (e.g., WD/JS/correlation L2, plus utility metrics if enabled) - `tstr_results.json` — TSTR utility results (only if --use-catboost and/or --use-mlp is enabled) To run DCR evalution, here is an example: ```bash python scripts/compute_dcr.py --dataset adult --exp ddpm_md4_smart_norm ``` Restore a compressed dataset Restores a compressed split (X_num_*, X_cat_*, y_*) back to the original column space using `compression_meta.json` + `feature_split_manifest.json`. Template and example: ```bash python scripts/restore_table.py --meta-dir [meta_dir] --data-dir [compressed_dir] --splits [train|val|test] --output-dir [out_dir] python scripts/restore_table.py --meta-dir adult_files --data-dir exp/compressed_adult/ddpm_md4_smart_norm --splits train --output-dir restored/compressed_adult_synth ``` Outputs: - `[out_dir]/train_restored.csv` (and/or val_restored.csv, test_restored.csv) Validate the restorer (round-trip check) Checks that restoration is consistent by re-encoding the restored CSV back into compressed arrays and comparing with the original .npy files. Template and example: ```bash python scripts/validate_restorer.py --meta-dir [meta_dir] --data-dir [compressed_dir] --csv [restored_csv] --split [train|val|test] python scripts/validate_restorer.py --meta-dir adult_files --data-dir exp/compressed_adult/ddpm_md4_smart_norm --csv restored/compressed_adult_synth/train_restored.csv --split train ``` Outputs: - Printed summary in the terminal (e.g., allclose/equal + mismatch counts).
